title: feat: web search, fetch, and citation UI
description:
## Summary

When a chat response cites web search/fetch results, users currently have
to parse inline citation text to know what was referenced. This PR renders
each citation as a compact aside pill next to the claim it supports, and
adds a single "Sources" pill per message that aggregates every citation
in that message so users can scan all sources at a glance without hunting
through the response.

This is built on top of #278's generic `<shiny-aside>` markup convention —
citations are just asides tagged with a `data-citation` marker, so as that
component evolves (interaction handling, styling, etc.) citations should
keep working without changes here. This PR stacks on #278 and will need
to be rebased once it merges.

## What's included

- Web search/fetch tool activity (query, results, fetch status) rendered
  as UI onto the shiny-aside base
- Citations deduped per message (same URL + rendered body only shown once)
- A message-scoped collector aggregates citations from all asides in a
  message into a "Sources" pill + popover, with favicons and titles
- Test coverage: unit (citation model/collector), component
  (SourcesSummary, dedupe plugin), and Playwright e2e

## Python only, for now — R is blocked on ellmer

The server-side half of this (chatlas web search/fetch/citation content →
`<shiny-web-search>` / `<shiny-web-fetch>` / `<shiny-aside data-citation>`
markup) currently only ships for Python. Porting it to R's `contents_shinychat()`
is blocked on gaps in ellmer 0.4.2:

- `ContentToolRequestSearch` / `ContentToolResponseSearch` / `ContentToolRequestFetch` /
  `ContentToolResponseFetch` exist in ellmer but aren't exported, so there's no
  public way to hook `contents_shinychat()` onto them.
- `ContentToolResponseSearch` only carries bare URLs, no titles.
- `ContentToolResponseFetch` has no normalized success/error status.
- Citations aren't a first-class content type in ellmer at all — they're parsed
  during streaming and then dropped when the final `ContentText` is built, so
  there's nothing to hook inline citation rendering onto.

None of this is filed upstream yet. Until it lands, R support for this feature
is a documented gap rather than something worked around with unexported-internals
access or provider-specific JSON parsing inside shinychat.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cd js && npm run lint && npm test`
- [ ] `uv run pytest` (Playwright web_citations suite)
- [ ] Manual: ask a chatlas-backed app to do a web search, confirm inline
      citation pills dedupe and the Sources pill lists all of them
